refnamediv.refpurpose: Computes principal component analysis for the data matrix X

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis:
comprinc = pca(X) [comprinc, score, lambda] = pca(X) [comprinc, score, lambda, tsquare] = pca(X) [comprinc, score, lambda, tsquare, explained, mu] = pca(X)
comprinc = pca(X, Name, Value) [comprinc, score, lambda] = pca(X, Name, Value) [comprinc, score, lambda, tsquare] = pca(X, Name, Value) [comprinc, score, lambda, tsquare, explained, mu] = pca(X, Name, Value)

listitem.para: is a nxp (n observations, p variables) real matrix.
'Algorithm': Algorithm used to compute the principal components. Possible values are: "svd" (default) and "eig"
'Centered': Boolean specifying whether variables are centered before computing the PCA. Default value: %t.
'Economy': Boolean, use to allow economy size singular value decomposition. This option is only used when Algorithm="svd". Default value: %t.

'NumComponents': Positive integer specifying the number of principal components to return. The outputs coeff, score, latent, explained and the Hotelling's T² statistic are computed using only these returned principal components. Default value: size(X, 2).
'Weights': Row vector of doubles of length size(X, 1) containing observation weights. Default value: ones(1, size(X, 1)).
'VariableWeights': A row positive vector of length size(X, 2) containing variable weights or the string "variance". Default value: [].
Matrix of size p x p (p is equal to size(X, 2)) whose columns are the principal component coefficients (principal directions).
n-by-p matrix or n-by-NumComponents matrix if 'NumComponents' is specified.
Each row corresponds to the projection of an observation onto the selected principal components.
Variance explained by each principal component (eigenvalues of the covariance matrix).
p-by-1 or NumComponents-by-1 (if 'NumComponents' is specified) vector.
a n column vector. Hotelling's T² statistic computed from the returned principal component scores.
a column vector of length "number of components". The percentage of variance explained by each principal component.
a row vector of length p. The estimated mean of each variable of X.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: pca performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the observations stored in the rows of X. The variables are assumed to be stored in the columns.
By default, the variables are centered before computing the principal components. The coefficients are returned as orthonormal vectors ordered according to decreasing explained variance.
The principal component scores are obtained by projecting the centered observations onto the principal component directions.

The Hotelling's T² statistic is computed from the principal component scores returned by the function. Consequently, when the "NumComponents" option is used, the T² statistic is evaluated in the reduced principal component subspace defined by the returned components.

listitem.para: "svd" (default): computes the principal components using the Singular Value Decomposition of the data matrix.

"eig": computes the principal components from the eigenvalue decomposition of the covariance matrix. When "NumComponents" is smaller than the number of variables, only the requested dominant eigenpairs are computed using eigs, which can significantly reduce the computation time for large data sets.

refsection.para: The "svd" and "eig" algorithms produce equivalent principal components up to numerical round-off errors. The "eig" algorithm can be advantageous when only a small number of principal components is requested.
To obtain the pca graph, use the show_pca function.

refsection.title: Examples

revdescription.para:
Improvements of the function:
"Economy", "Centered", "NumComponents", "Weights" and "VariableWeights" options are added.
Returns now the percentage of the variance explained by each principal component and the estimated mean of each variable of X.
Warning, there is an incompatibility with previous versions: the order of the first three output arguments have changed.
The old [lambda, comprinc, scores] = pca(x) syntax has been replaced by [comprinc, scores, lambda] = pca(x). In previous versions, pca only computed the principal components with standardized variables. To obtain the same results, use "VariableWeights" option with "variance" value: [comprinc, scores, lambda] = pca(x, "VariableWeights", "variance"). In this case, comprinc is not orthonormal. You can compute the orthonormal coefficient thanks to diag(stdev(x))\comprinc. An other possibility is to use wcenter function i.e, [comprinc, scores, lambda] = pca(wcenter(x, 1)). A warning is displayed when pca is called with 1, 2 or 3 output arguments. To avoid the warning to be displayed, call pca with at least four output arguments (e.g. [comprinc, scores, lambda, _] = pca()).
Note that lambda is a column vector containing the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of x. To obtain the ratio of the corresponding eigenvalue over the sum of eigenvalues, use the following formula: lambda(:, 1) / sum(lambda(:, 1))
Algorithm option added. Possible values are "svd" and "eigs".
